title: The Mississippi curves through New Orleans
caption: Aerial view of New Orleans and the Mississippi River, April 2007. Geographic context for Bulbancha’s longer history, not an image of the place before colonization.

title: The Port of New Orleans
caption: A container ship at the Napoleon Avenue terminal, April 2007. A modern view illustrating the port’s continuing function; the Louisiana Purchase occurred in 1803.

title: Congo Square — modern view
caption: A modern photograph of Congo Square. It shows the place, not a reconstruction of its early gatherings.

title: A slave-auction advertisement, 1856
caption: A New Orleans auction broadside dated February 23, 1856, naming people offered for sale. Primary-source evidence of slavery and the city’s trade in human beings; its dehumanizing language is historical evidence.
credit: J.A. Beard & May, New Orleans, slave auctioneers. Bulletin Print, 35 Gravier St., New Orleans

title: Mardi Gras morning in Tremé
caption: A Tremé neighborhood street on Mardi Gras morning, February 13, 2018. Contemporary place and cultural context rather than a scene from the beginnings of jazz.

title: King Oliver, circa 1915
caption: Historical portrait of jazz musician King Oliver, circa 1915. Oliver’s work connects the New Orleans story to the movement of jazz and Louis Armstrong’s career.

title: Hurricane Katrina from space
caption: NASA satellite image of Hurricane Katrina on August 28, 2005. A view of the storm itself, not a photograph of damage or recovery in New Orleans.

title: A living parade tradition
caption: Participants in the Big 9 parade on St. Claude Avenue, New Orleans, December 21, 2008. A specific example of the city’s continuing public musical culture.
